[warm, explaining calmly across a table] Say your union asks for average pay by grade, and a month later one reporter joins and you ask again. Both tables hide any group smaller than three, so they look safe. But subtract one from the other, and you get her exact salary: seventy thousand euros.

[pause] Bandsheet is built to stop exactly that.

So a member drops in the payslip email their payroll sent. NEAR AI Cloud reads it inside a confidential GPU, and we check its attestation before anything is sent. The entry is sealed in the browser to a key that only exists inside an OutLayer enclave, and it goes on chain without gas.

Now, if someone edits even one digit, it doesn't count. The chapel voted on NEAR to trust the employer's D-K-I-M key, and the enclave checks every signature.

When the chapel asks for a release through its Sputnik DAO, the enclave replays every earlier table and solves the attacker's equations first. So it publishes four bands, withholds the Senior one, and writes why to NEAR.

We ran a hundred generated attacks. A typical tool leaked salaries in ninety-five of them. Bandsheet leaked none, and you can check that yourself with one command.

Reps can ask Bandsheet questions from Claude through an M-C-P tool, and every member sees where they stand next to the E-U median, with an Article 7 request ready to send.

[pause] That's Bandsheet: every band published, and nobody exposed.
